definitions.gloss: dust; fine particles; particulate matter; airborne dust
definitions.explanation: Very small solid particles suspended in the air, often a health or safety concern in workplaces and environments.

examples.japanese: {工場|こうじょう}で{粉|ふん}じんが{発生|はっせい}している。
examples.english: Dust is being generated at the factory.

examples.japanese: {粉|ふん}じんを{吸|す}い{込|こ}まないようにマスクをつけてください。
examples.english: Please wear a mask to avoid inhaling dust particles.

examples.japanese: {黄砂|こうさ}による{粉|ふん}じんの{濃度|のうど}が{高|たか}くなっているため、{外出|がいしゅつ}を{控|ひか}えてください。
examples.english: Since the dust concentration from yellow sand is high, please refrain from going outside.

notes:
Written as {粉塵|ふんじん} in full kanji or {粉|ふん}じん in mixed script (the latter is more common in general media, as {塵|じん} is not a {常用漢字|じょうようかんじ}). Refers specifically to airborne particulate matter, not everyday household dust.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {粉|ふん}じん{濃度|のうど} — dust concentration
- {粉|ふん}じん{爆発|ばくはつ} — dust explosion
- {粉|ふん}じん{対策|たいさく} — dust countermeasures
- {粉|ふん}じんを{吸|す}い{込|こ}む — to inhale dust particles

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ほこり — dust (everyday household dust)
- {微粒子|びりゅうし} — fine particles (more scientific/technical)
- PM2.5 — fine particulate matter (specific size classification)
- {砂|すな}ぼこり — sand dust (blown by wind)

USAGE:
A technical term commonly encountered in workplace safety regulations, environmental reports, and weather advisories (especially regarding {黄砂|こうさ} — yellow sand from China). Industrial {粉|ふん}じん exposure is regulated under Japanese occupational health laws.
